A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Moral Alignment for LLM Agents. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM fine-tuning experiments, learning dynamics, moral-regret measurements, and generalization and robustness evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds prompt-variation experiments, value-prompted baseline comparisons, and qualitative follow-up responses.

M1.justification: Both versions use Gemma2-2b-it with PPO and LoRA, the same intrinsic reward functions and illegal-action penalty, and the same sequential fine-tuning schedules. The added appendix experiments evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: The five matrix games and training-opponent coverage are retained. v2 adds a household-cleaning scenario without numerical payoffs and a small evaluation of models' verbal decision justifications (Sections 8.10 and 8.12), modestly extending scenario and task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 8.11 and Figure 25 add Deontological and Utilitarian value-prompted base models to the five-game comparison. These introduce prompting-only alignment alternatives absent from v1, which compared the unmodified base model and different fine-tuning reward schedules.

E3.justification: v2 adds systematic payoff-matrix row/column permutations, comparisons across prompt formats, and contextual follow-up-question procedures. The unrelated-prompt evaluation changes from original action1/action2 tokens in v1 Figure 15 to reported action3/action4 tokens in v2 Figure 18, although Section 8.8 retains the older description. Core training budgets and the main evaluation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the earlier token-reversal checks with four payoff-order permutations, structured versus prose and nonnumeric prompt tests, and qualitative decision-explanation cases (Sections 8.9, 8.10, and 8.12). Several LLM-trained counterparts of the earlier appendix prompt and token-robustness analyses are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds, averages, and 95% confidence intervals for the quantitative experiments. The disclosure excluding occasional nonconvergent runs is unchanged. v2 does not introduce a new statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New results report sensitivity to reversing both payoff-matrix axes, weaker transfer without explicit payoffs, failure of the value-prompted baselines to produce legal actions, and example verbal justifications. Unrelated-prompt and reciprocity response profiles are revised, and several LLM-trained appendix result panels disappear. Main Figures 4–5 retain their results; the revised prompt conditions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The reward definitions in Table 1, moral-regret definition in Section 5.1, and game payoff matrices are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims about intrinsic-reward alignment, unlearning selfish strategies, and generalization across games. The added evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's token-semantic and Utilitarian-transfer limitations, v2 introduces matrix-position dependence as a possible mechanism, suggests pretraining familiarity may explain paraphrased-scenario behavior, and reports no explicit moral justification in the sampled explanations. These additions materially qualify the interpretation and boundaries of apparent moral generalization.

D1.justification: v2 supplies additional permutation, natural-language, value-prompting, and follow-up prompt templates in Figures 9–10, 24, and 26. Training hyperparameters, package versions, and the promise to release code upon acceptance remain unchanged. Some added templates inconsistently mix action1/action2 instructions with action3/action4 payoff labels.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged, as is the positioning relative to RLHF, DPO, prior intrinsic moral rewards, and social-dilemma research. The new prompting baselines do not introduce cited comparison methods or revised novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the intended meaning of unlearning in a footnote, adds a flatmate example, revises some captions, and reorganizes and extends the appendix subsections. The main narrative, abstract, discussion, and conclusion remain largely unchanged; the additions do not constitute extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 move legends outside the training plots. The appendix adds substantial prompt, permutation, baseline, and follow-up displays, including a response table presented as Figure 27. Several existing multi-panel figures are reduced to TFT-trained results, alongside extensive figure relocation and regrouping.

improvement.justification: The added controls and baselines address important gaps in v1's generalization evidence. However, v2 replaces the unrelated-prompt plots while retaining Section 8.8's original-token description, and new permutation and baseline examples mix incompatible action labels. These inconsistencies leave the precise experimental conditions uncertain, limiting confidence in the added evidence. Together with the removal of several LLM-trained checks, they prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
